title: The Relics of General Chasse: A Tale of Antwerp

cognitive_validation.rationale: There is no imaginary science or novel social organization to validate; the object operates by ordinary means. The dimension is moot because no novum is present.

novum_candidates.description: The 'relics of General Chasse' are fragments of a pair of black trousers (an undergarment/breeches) cut up and distributed as needle-cases, pen-wipers, pin-cushions, and slippers, mistakenly believed to be venerable relics of a famous general but actually belonging to Mr. Horne.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The comic reversal—ordinary garments mistaken for venerable relics, then revealed as an ordinary gentleman's trousers—creates humor, not cognitive estrangement in Suvin's sense. No empirical norm is altered.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The relics do drive the entire plot and comic resolution, but centrality alone does not create a novum absent novelty and cognitive validation.

novelty.rationale: This is a comic mundane object (a cut-up pair of trousers) within an ordinary 19th-century realist social setting. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from empirical reality; the story universe is entirely our own.
